content_of_post_to_comment:
I'm about to go to college soon and I'm just now realizing how utterly unmotivated and lazy I am. My entire life I've never had to do anything but school, yet I'm still failing at that. I'm 16 and don't know how to cook, clean, wash clothes, make food, or get myself up in the morning. I thought I'd grow out of it but I'm just as incompetent and dysfunctional as I was years ago. I can't imagine myself doing well in school, holding a job, or even keeping myself alive.

I've ruled out most things that could be causing my laziness, I'm on prozac for depression, stimulants for ADHD, and I'm in therapy. There's nothing else to change except for myself.

But I just can't force myself to make any change. No matter how embarrassed or guilty I feel having my own mother clean my room, I don't do anything. I try starting small but even that's incredibly difficult. If I'm too lazy to feed myself how could I possibly start making routines? Where do I start?

TL;DR Is it possible to fix myself before I fuck up my life for good?
comment: You’re 16, not a failed adult. And being on medication and in therapy doesn’t mean every struggle is something you can fix by trying harder. If even feeding yourself feels impossible, that’s worth telling your therapist exactly as you described it here. You don’t need to become fully independent before college; you need support figuring out why basic tasks feel so overwhelming, not more guilt piled on top.
